title: feat(transcode): quality tiers, size estimates, and actual size in the completion notification

leads.summary: A symlinked video always gets false 'larger than source' estimates
leads.consequence: A video reached through a symlink passes -f and ffprobe reads the target, but stat measures the length of the symlink itself. For a 120 MiB target reached via link.mov, all three quality choices say 'larger than source' instead of ~41/~23/~11 MB. The selected tier still encodes and reports the finished output size; a second run dedupes its existing output, but the user never sees useful pre-encode size estimates on this common file shape. Follow symlinks in the source size lookup with stat -Lc %s -- on the quoted input, and exercise a symlink fixture with the actual stat.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus (opus/followup-1.md): with default file(1) a symlinked input is rejected by media_type before select_quality in base and head, so unreachable by default; not published

leads.summary: Manual promises size estimates for animated GIF choices that are never computed
leads.consequence: The new manual presents a quality prompt 'for videos, with a rough estimate of how big each choice will come out', then says the finished notification can be compared with the estimate. A GIF is a video choice, but GIF quality rows show 15/10/5 fps only, do not run ffprobe and have no estimated bytes. Explicit positional quality also skips the menu, and MP4 falls back to qualitative rows if probing fails. Readers choosing GIF should be told they get frame rates rather than sizes. Narrow the size-estimate promise to interactive MP4 when metadata is available.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus minor note; published in Smaller notes

leads.summary: Open #6698's directory transcoding conflicts with this PR's single-file quality pipeline
leads.consequence: The two heads are diverged, and merging their scripts gives three conflict hunks (metadata, help and main video arm). #6698 introduces transcode_file(input,format,resolution) and a directory arm which calls transcode_video with four args and output_path with three. Here the quality tier is passed as the fourth output_path and fifth transcode_video argument, and the quality prompt is in main after format/resolution. If #6698's single-file transcode_file arm wins when resolving the conflict, non-default requested qualities revert to medium and lose their suffix. #6698's directory and Nautilus multi-file paths also have no shared-quality selection. Integrate the two pipelines and test both PRs' workflows together; this is a merge-integration risk, not a defect on either isolated head.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus #1 and related PRs; published

leads.summary: Open #11057 reuses the same menu-select payload argument slot as --default-index
leads.consequence: Both PRs are diverged and bin/omarchy-menu-select has three conflict hunks; the QML side merges without markers. This PR gives Perl $ARGV[6] to defaultIndex, while #11057 gives that exact $ARGV[6] to multiSelect. A straightforward keep-both resolution sets multiSelect true for every transcode quality picker passing --default-index 1, and can make defaultIndex 1 for multi-select callers. #11057's multi-mode repurposes Tab to tick rather than navigate, and confirming multiple tiers yields a newline-containing selection rejected by select_quality. Merge must allocate distinct argv slots and test both flags together, not simply keep both Perl assignments.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus related PRs; published (wording marked as from conflict hunks)

leads.summary: Open #12363 adds a different test at this PR's new menu-select-test.sh path
leads.consequence: The two heads are diverged. #12363 adds --print-index to the same binary and independently adds test/shell.d/menu-select-test.sh. Merging by choosing either new test file silently drops the other's suite: the default-index/nonfinite tests here or the --print-index inverse-mapping tests there. Git merge-file shows conflicts in both bin/omarchy-menu-select and the entire new test file. Combine both test bodies and parser changes; test/shell auto-discovers only one file with that name.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus related PRs; published

leads.summary: Two further open PRs conflict with the transcode and menu test integration points
leads.location: bin/omarchy-transcode, bin/omarchy-menu-select, shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js, test/shell.d/menu-test.sh; related #7320 and #7610
leads.consequence: #7320 changes the empty file-pick error path in transcode and the menu-select header. comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the encoder side matches the description. On a synthetic clip, explicit `medium` and an omitted quality with `medium` picked both produce the same ffmpeg argv as the base script, and the output packets are identical. The high/low tiers use the stated CRF and fps values. The `omarchy-menu-select` guard works: on the base script `--width 1e1000` emits `"width":Inf` and hangs, while at head it emits `0`, and `defaultIndex` is floored and clamped in `MenuModel.js`. The three changed test files pass at head and fail against the base code, and the full `test/shell` suite has the same six environment-dependent failures on base and head. The branch merges cleanly onto the current `quattro` tip.

Two behaviour changes are worth a look: a command that already names format and resolution now stops at a quality menu, and the completion message for small outputs is cut off.

### A command that names format and resolution now opens a quality menu

`main` prompts for quality whenever the input is a video and the 4th positional is empty (`bin/omarchy-transcode:411-413`). Before this PR, a three-argument video command ran without any menu.

| `omarchy transcode clip.mp4 mp4 720p` | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Menus shown | none | `Select quality` (after two ffprobe calls) |
| Esc on that menu | n/a | exits non-zero, no output, no notification |
| Medium picked | n/a | same argv and file name as base |

The PR's own test reflects this: every three-argument video run in `transcode-quality-test.sh` sets `FAKE_PICK`.

**Impact:** the three-argument form is documented as the form for when you already know what you want, and it now blocks until the shell menu answers:
- The help text says `Videos: high, medium, low (default: medium)` (`bin/omarchy-transcode:31`).
- The manual calls `omarchy transcode ~/Videos/demo.mov mp4 1080p` the form for when "you already know what you want" and says "leave it off and you get the same file as before".
- The agent skill line in `default/agents/skills/omarchy/capture.md` and the `omarchy:examples` three-argument example point scripts and agents at this form.
- Open PR #6698 asks format and resolution once for a Nautilus batch, then runs `omarchy-transcode <path> "$format" "$resolution"` per file. With this PR, each video in a multi-file batch would ask for quality separately.

**Suggested change:** when format and resolution both came from arguments, use `medium` without a menu, so the prompt appears only in the interactive flow. If the prompt is intended, drop "(default: medium)" from the help text and describe the prompt in the manual and the skill line.

### Outputs under 1 MiB show a truncated completion message

`output_size_label` prints `<1 MB` (`bin/omarchy-transcode:296`), so the body becomes `Saved and copied to clipboard (<1 MB).` The notification card renders bodies with `textFormat: Text.StyledText` (`shell/plugins/notifications/components/NotificationCard.qml`), and `NotificationLogic.styledBody` passes this body through unchanged. Qt's StyledText parser treats `<` as the start of a tag that runs to the next `>`, or to the end of the string when there is none, so everything from `<` on is dropped.

Measured with Qt 6.11.2 (offscreen `Text` widths):

| Body text | Width | Rendered |
|---|---|---|
| `Saved and copied to clipboard (<1 MB).` | 280.98 | same width as `Saved and copied to clipboard (` alone |
| Same string as PlainText | 351.50 | full text |
| `Saved and copied to clipboard (<1 MB).` | 351.50 | full text |
| `Saved and copied to clipboard (38 MB).` | equal in both formats | full text |

A real sub-1 MiB encode at head sent exactly the `(<1 MB).` body. The PR test pins that literal string, so it cannot catch the rendering.

**Impact:** short clips and small pictures finish with `Saved and copied to clipboard (`.

**Suggested change:** prefer wording without `<`, for example `under 1 MB`, which renders the same with any notification server (escaping as `<1 MB` also works in Omarchy's own card). Update the test string to match.

### Name collisions now get `-2`, `-3` suffixes, which the description calls unchanged

The base `output_path` has no collision handling; the suffix loop was added in this PR (commit `f523e4d`). What changes on a repeat run with the same settings:

| Existing output | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Picture | `magick` overwrites it | writes `-2`, keeps the old file |
| Video, no terminal | ffmpeg declines to overwrite and exits 0, so the old file's URI is copied and the toast says "Saved" | writes `-2`, keeps the old file |

**Impact:** for videos this fixes a false success. For pictures, repeat runs now accumulate copies instead of replacing the file.

**Suggested change:** describe the `-N` naming in the PR description and the manual, and state the picture behaviour change so maintainers can decide on it.

### Smaller notes

- **Validation order:** format and resolution are checked after both prompts (`bin/omarchy-transcode:379-409`). `clip.mp4 avi 1080p` now fails before any menu or toast, as described, but `clip.mp4 avi` still shows the resolution menu first. Checking the format right after `media_type` would close that gap.
- **Pictures with a 4th argument:** any 4th positional on a picture now fails with "quality applies to videos only"; base ignored it.
- **Units:** estimates and the finished size divide by 1,048,576 but print "MB". Files (Nautilus, via GLib `g_format_size`) uses 1000-based units, so a 39,845,888-byte file reads 38 MB in the toast and 39.8 MB in Files.
- **Manual wording:** it says each video quality choice comes with a size estimate, but gif rows show fps only, and mp4 falls back to qualitative labels when probing fails.
- **Optional test improvement:** `test/shell.d/menu-select-test.sh:129-134` fails if any other script in `bin/` ever passes `--default-index`, so a legitimate new caller of the flag would break the suite. Asserting only that `omarchy-transcode` passes the flag keeps the pin without that side effect.
- **Planning references in shipped comments:** `D-00a`, `D-04`, `T-05-01`, `WR-01` and "Phase 6" in the tests, and "the PR #6698 conflict window" in `bin/omarchy-transcode`, mean nothing outside the author's notes.

### Related open PRs

- **#6698** (folder transcoding): conflicts in `bin/omarchy-transcode`, and its batch design is affected by the first finding.
- **#11057** (`--multi`) and **#11877** (`--keep-open`): both also take Perl `$ARGV[6]` in `omarchy-menu-select`, the slot this PR uses for `defaultIndex`. The conflict hunks assign both values to that one slot, so whichever lands second needs a new slot.
- **#12363** (`--print-index`): adds its own `test/shell.d/menu-select-test.sh`. Picking either side of that add/add conflict drops the other suite.
- **#13043**: adds `initialIndex` for menu mode, while this PR adds `defaultIndex` for select mode. Aligning the names may be worth it.
- **#7320**, **#7610**, **#7954** and **#11580** also have textual conflicts with this branch in files it changes.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `b9535ec` against the base script, its callers (keybinding, menu action, Nautilus extension), the menu and notification QML, and upstream Qt, FFmpeg and GLib source. The PR tests, related tests, the full `test/shell` suite and behaviour probes with real ffmpeg, ffprobe and ImageMagick on synthetic media ran in an isolated sandbox, with the menu, notification and clipboard stubbed. StyledText rendering was measured offscreen. The menu pre-highlight and the notification were not viewed on a live desktop. Conflicts with other open PRs are from pairwise merges of the public branches.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
